title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 9-11), 'Galois axiomatique': Grothendieck defines a category C 'with profinite automorphism groups'. Each Aut(X) is a profinite group, and for every u in Hom(X,Y) the stabilizer G_u of u, under the action (psi,phi)·u = phi u psi^{-1} of Aut(X)×Aut(Y), is closed. Hom(X,Y) is then topologized as the topological sum of its orbits. Each orbit carries the quotient topology of the homogeneous space (Aut(X)×Aut(Y))/G_u, which is profinite, so Hom(X,Y) is locally compact. He wants composition (14), Hom(X,Y)×Hom(Y,Z)→Hom(X,Z), to be continuous. On the previous page this was reduced, for a product of two orbits, to continuity of (g,f,g',f') ↦ (g'vf'^{-1})(guf^{-1}).

On this page:
1. The outer factors g' and f^{-1} act continuously by construction of the orbit topology. So continuity reduces to that of (15), Aut(Y)→Hom(X,Z), phi ↦ v phi u, for fixed u and v.
2. Take G_u = {(psi,phi) : phi u = u psi}, a closed subgroup of Aut(X)×Aut(Y). The composite G_u → (pr_2) Aut(Y) → Hom(X,Z) equals (psi,phi) ↦ v u psi. This is continuous because psi ↦ w psi is continuous on the orbit of w = vu.
3. Hence (15) is continuous on H_u = pr_2(G_u). The topology of H_u is the quotient of that of G_u; this agrees with the subspace topology by compactness.
4. On a left translate alpha_i H_u, use v(alpha_i phi)u = (v alpha_i) u psi, the same argument with v replaced by v alpha_i. So (15) is continuous on every left coset of H_u.
5. Hypothesis (16)(*): for every u : X→Y, H_u has finite index in Aut_C(Y). Under it, finitely many cosets cover Aut(Y). Being closed of finite index, they are open (first marginal NB), so (15), hence (14), is continuous.

Second marginal NB, as I read it: (16) is equivalent to saying that each Aut(X)×Aut(Y)-orbit in Hom(X,Y) is a finite union of Aut(X)-orbits. Indeed, Aut(Y) permutes transitively the Aut(X)-orbits inside the orbit of u, and the stabilizer of u·Aut(X) is exactly H_u. This is what lets the next page write the completed Hom as the completion with respect to Aut(X) alone (formula 17).

Purpose: (16) is a purely combinatorial condition. The next page uses it to construct a 'profinite envelope' Ĉ_0 of an abstract category C_0, completing automorphism groups and Hom-sets compatibly with composition. This is evidently aimed at a profinite completion of the Teichmüller groupoid/tower, on which Gal(Q̄/Q) should act.
errors: The text says 'd'où la continuité de (14), donc de (15)'. Logically it is continuity of (15) on all cosets that yields (14); the order is inverted. This is a slip, not a mathematical error.

Implicit: the quotient topology on H_u (from G_u) must agree with the subspace topology from Aut(Y) for the gluing argument. This holds because G_u is compact and Aut(Y) is Hausdorff. Also, a closed finite-index subgroup is open, so its cosets form a finite open cover; this is noted in the margin.
Without (16) the argument fails: if H_u has infinite index, the cosets are closed but not open. So (16) is a genuine hypothesis, not a technicality.

ideas.what: Topologizing Hom-sets of a category with profinite automorphism groups as disjoint unions of homogeneous spaces (Aut X × Aut Y)/G_u, and proving continuity of composition
ideas.modern_name: category enriched in (locally) profinite spaces; profinite groupoid/category structures; cf. infinite Galois categories / Noohi groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Galois categories: Grothendieck, SGA1 (1961); infinite and topological variants: Noohi (2008), Bhatt–Scholze (2015); profinite categories in semigroup theory: Almeida, Jones
ideas.where_published: SGA1 V treats Galois categories with finite Hom-sets; this orbit-topology axiomatics is not in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Finiteness condition (16): the image H_u of the stabilizer of u in Aut(Y) has finite index, equivalently each Aut(X)×Aut(Y)-orbit in Hom(X,Y) is a finite union of Aut(X)-orbits
ideas.modern_name: orbit-finiteness / 'finite index' condition ensuring the profinite completion of a category or groupoid is well-behaved
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; similar conditions appear implicitly in profinite completions of the Teichmüller tower (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Boggi, Nakamura–Schneps) and in orbit categories
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces the profinite Teichmüller tower and the Galois action on it; this axiom is not stated there

ideas.what: Reduction of continuity of composition to a coset-by-coset argument via the stabilizer G_u
ideas.modern_name: standard argument with homogeneous spaces of profinite groups

missed.claim: An axiomatic framework, 'Galois axiomatique', for profinite completion of a whole category, not just a groupoid: completing Aut(X) and Hom(X,Y) compatibly under the purely combinatorial hypothesis (16). It is intended for the Teichmüller tower with its non-invertible maps. Grothendieck notes on the previous page that it 'mérite d'être fait avec plus de soin'. The literature completes Teichmüller groupoids and mapping class groups, but I know of no general published treatment of completing categories with non-invertible morphisms under exactly this finite-index condition.
missed.quote: (16) (*) Pour toute flèche u : X → Y dans C, l'image H_u dans Aut_C(Y) du groupe G_u des couples de flèches ... est un sous-groupe d'indice fini [de] Aut(Y).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a general recipe for 'profinite envelopes' of categories, relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, to completing operads or modular categories that include non-invertible morphisms, and to anabelian functoriality. It could be compared with Noohi's and Bhatt–Scholze's infinite Galois categories and with Boavida–Horel–Robertson's profinite completion of operads.

deep.surprise_reason: The argument itself is routine point-set topology for profinite groups. What is mildly notable is the explicit axiom (16), with its reformulation as finiteness of Aut(X)-orbits inside Aut(X)×Aut(Y)-orbits. It serves as the hinge for a general profinite completion of categories aimed at the Teichmüller tower, a framework Grothendieck never published.
transcription_corrections: The phrase 'continue sur tous ceux [?] dans l'image' is probably 'continue sur (l'image de G_u)', i.e. continuous on H_u, with the inserted note that H_u ⊂ Aut(Y).
The line 'et on peut [?], donc aussi sur H_u voisinages [?]' probably means 'et par suite, donc aussi sur les translatés'. The insertion 'α_i H_u (α_i ∈ Aut(Y))' names the left cosets.
'grâce à l'[?]' is likely 'grâce à l'identité v(α_iφ)u = vα_i u ψ'.
'd'où la continuité de (14), donc de (15)': the manuscript's '(14)' may be a misread of (15). Logically (15) implies (14).
First margin: 'NB H_u est un sous-groupe fermé de Aut(Y), donc il est ouvert ssi il est d'indice fini...' is correct as read.
Second margin: probably 'NB l'hypothèse (16) équivaut à : pour tout u ∈ Hom(X,Y), l'orbite de u sous Aut(X)×Aut(Y) est réunion d'un nombre fini d'orbites sous Aut(X)'. 'Aut D(X)' is a misreading.
The bracket '(16) {(*)' at the bottom left labels hypothesis (16) as (*), the condition referred to on the next page.
